text:
simEventData() fully general, common settings package provides ready-made wrappers built top . simSurvData() simulates survival data individuals risk censoring (0) event (1). default covariate effects:  can specify baseline covariates L0 A0 affect censoring event hazards beta matrix, set Weibull shape (\eta) scale (
u) parameters:  simCRdata() simulates data competing risk setting two competing causes, using kind parameters simSurvData():  simDisease() simulates health care data setting patients can experience three events: Censoring (0), Death (1), Disease (2). beta_X_Y arguments control X affects Y: positive value means higher value X increases intensity Y, negative value decreases . See ?simDisease() full list arguments.  simTreatment() extends disease setting treatment process: simulates four event types representing censoring (0), death (1), treatment (2), covariate change (3), controlled via beta_X_Y arguments:  simDropIn() related wrapper setting 4 5 events: censoring, death, drop-initiation, covariate change, optionally treatment. configured beta_X_Y arguments; see ?simDropIn() details. simEventTV() adapts simEventData() allow effects change fixed time point: time t_prime, matrix tv_eff added beta. flexibility comes cost slightly slower simulation procedure, use simEventData() instead effects constant time.  Sometimes intensity event depend just covariates event counts, time elapsed since recent occurrence event. Assume event-specific intensity form    \lambda^x(t \mid \mathcal F_t)   = R^x(t \mid \mathcal F_t) \,\eta^x 
u^x t^{
u^x-1} \,\phi^x(t \mid \mathcal F_t),     \phi^x(t \mid \mathcal F_t)   = \exp\left( L^	op  eta_1 + (T^* - t) eta_2 ight),  T^* denotes recent event time. Simulation setting done using simEventDataTdPhi(), takes additional argument beta2 controlling exponential decay/growth \phi^x:
code: data <- simSurvData(100) plotEventData(data, title = "Survival Data") # Effects of L0 and A0 on the censoring hazard (1st column) and death hazard (2nd column) beta <- cbind("Censoring" = c(0, 0), "Death" = c(1, -1)) eta <- c(0.2, 0.2) nu <- c(1.05, 1.05)  data <- simSurvData(100, beta = beta, eta = eta, nu = nu) plotEventData(data, title = "Survival Data") data <- simCRdata(100) plotEventData(data, title = "Competing Risk Data") data <- simDisease(   N = 100,   cens = 1,   eta = c(0.1, 0.3, 0.1),   nu = c(1.1, 1.3, 1.1),   beta_L0_L = 1,   beta_A0_L = -1.1,   beta_L_D = 1,   beta_L0_D = 0 )  plotEventData(data, title = "Disease data") data <- simTreatment(   N = 100,   beta_L_A = 1,   beta_L_D = 1,   beta_A_D = -1,   beta_A_L = -0.5,   beta_L0_A = 1,   eta = rep(0.1, 4),   nu = rep(1.1, 4),   followup = 5,   cens = 1,   op = 1 )  plotEventData(data, title = "Treatment setting") set.seed(6258) eta <- rep(0.1, 4) term_deltas <- c(0, 1) tv_eff <- matrix(0.5, ncol = 4, nrow = 6) beta <- matrix(nrow = 6, ncol = 4, 0.5) t_prime <- 1  data <- simEventTV(   N = 100,   t_prime = t_prime,   tv_eff = tv_eff,   eta = eta,   term_deltas = term_deltas,   beta = beta,   lower = 10^(-15),   upper = 10^2,   max_events = 30 )  plotEventData(data) beta <- matrix(rnorm(4 * 6, 0, 0.1), ncol = 4) data <- simEventDataTdPhi(   N = 100,   beta2 = c(0.01, 2, 0, 0.1),   beta = beta,   upper = 10^20,   max_iter = 10^3 ) plotEventData(data)

what: Intensities Depending on Time Since Last Event with simEventDataTdPhi()
title: Getting Started with simevent
text: Sometimes intensity event depend just covariates event counts, time elapsed since recent occurrence event. Assume event-specific intensity form    \lambda^x(t \mid \mathcal F_t)   = R^x(t \mid \mathcal F_t) \,\eta^x \nu^x t^{\nu^x-1} \,\phi^x(t \mid \mathcal F_t),     \phi^x(t \mid \mathcal F_t)   = \exp\left( L^\top \beta_1 + (T^* - t)\beta_2 \right),  T^* denotes recent event time. Simulation setting done using simEventDataTdPhi(), takes additional argument beta2 controlling exponential decay/growth \phi^x:
code: beta <- matrix(rnorm(4 * 6, 0, 0.1), ncol = 4) data <- simEventDataTdPhi(   N = 100,   beta2 = c(0.01, 2, 0, 0.1),   beta = beta,   upper = 10^20,   max_iter = 10^3 ) plotEventData(data)

what: Simulating New Data from a Fitted Model
title: Getting Started with simevent
text: Besides simulating user-specified parameters, simevent can simulate new data model already fitted observed data. simEventCox() Cox proportional hazards models, simEventObj() model equipped predict2 method. Say observed data: Fit Cox models events interest, pass fitted models simEventCox(): New baseline covariates simulated resampling rows old_vars. simEventObj() works fitted model, long equip predict2() method returning times cumulative hazard new covariate values. example, Cox model:
code: set.seed(373) beta <- matrix(c(0.5, -1, -0.5, 0.5, 0, 0.5), ncol = 3, nrow = 2) data <- simCRdata(N = 1000, beta = beta) cox1 <- coxph(Surv(Time, Delta == 1) ~ L0 + A0, data = data) cox2 <- coxph(Surv(Time, Delta == 2) ~ L0 + A0, data = data)  cox_fits <- list("Process 1" = cox1, "Process 2" = cox2) old_vars <- data[, c(4, 5)] new_data <- simEventCox(100, cox_fits, old_vars = old_vars) head(new_data) #> Key: <ID> #>       ID      Time Delta        L0    A0 Process 1 Process 2 #>    <int>     <num> <num>     <num> <num>     <num>     <num> #> 1:     1 0.4931728     1 0.5363954     0         0         1 #> 2:     1 4.0046486     0 0.5363954     0         1         1 #> 3:     2 0.6828662     1 0.3144497     0         0         1 #> 4:     2 9.8772172     0 0.3144497     0         1         1 #> 5:     3 0.8909987     1 0.9335247     1         0         1 #> 6:     3 4.2916262     0 0.9335247     1         1         1 cox_fit <- coxph(Surv(Time, Delta == 1) ~ L0 + A0, data = data)  predict2 <- function(obj, ...) UseMethod("predict2") predict2.coxph <- function(obj, sim_data, ...) {   preds <- survfit(obj, newdata = sim_data)   # preds$cumhaz is a times x individuals matrix; reshape to individuals x times x events   chf <- array(t(preds$cumhaz), dim = c(nrow(sim_data), length(preds$time), 1))   list(time = preds$time, chf = chf) }  old_vars <- data[, c("L0", "A0")] new_data <- simEventObj(100, cox_fit, old_vars = old_vars) head(new_data) #> Key: <ID> #>       ID      Time Delta          L0    A0    N0 #>    <int>     <num> <num>       <num> <num> <num> #> 1:     1       Inf     0 0.926276597     0     0 #> 2:     2       Inf     0 0.730683018     0     0 #> 3:     3 13.181177     1 0.057044588     0     1 #> 4:     4  8.531944     1 0.006538616     1     1 #> 5:     5  1.371236     1 0.921506565     1     1 #> 6:     6  4.866903     1 0.240172203     0     1

code: # The observed data data_obs <- simDisease(N = 1000) data_obs <- IntFormatData(data_obs, N_cols = 6)  # Fit Cox models cox_death <- survival::coxph(survival::Surv(tstart, tstop, Delta == 1) ~ L0 + A0 + L, data = data_obs) cox_Disease <- survival::coxph(survival::Surv(tstart, tstop, Delta == 2) ~ L0 + A0, data = data_obs[L == 0])  # Then simulate new data: cox_fits <- list("D" = cox_death, "L" = cox_Disease) old_vars <- data_obs[, c("L0", "A0")] new_data <- simEventCox(100, cox_fits = cox_fits, old_vars = old_vars)
